Spot.doc: A named spot on the map; features find their place by name.

Feature.doc: Sizes of a spot's ground feature: radius, height, depth (m). A rectangle uses the marker's own size.

Path.doc: Paths from this marker to the markers it names.

District.doc: A district: the marker's box (its size, x by z). Lower order wins where boxes overlap; kind 'bounds' is the map's edge.

Plot.doc: A house plot: the marker's size is the footprint (x by z) and its yaw the door side; upper: must have an upper floor.

Hangout.doc: Where villagers hang out (marker kind 'trip': a far destination reached over the navmesh).

Clear.doc: Keep trees, bushes and rocks this far from here.

Block.doc: A static collider filling the marker's box (round: an upright cylinder, its size x the diameter), its y above the ground; on: stand on that entity's ground instead of its own (a crane on a slope).

Entrance.doc: A way into the underground: kind manhole, cellar_door or trapdoor; you come up facing the marker's yaw.

Hole.doc: A hole in the ground: the marker's box (x by z, turned by its yaw), or a circle its width across (round); its lining goes depth metres down from lip above the floor. On a map with its own flat floor (New York), the marker's height is the floor.

Spin.doc: Turns about its own up axis, rpm turns a minute (put it on a fan rotor's prefab instance; negative turns the other way).

Lamp.doc: A point light at the marker: lumens and reach (m); r, g, b its colour (all 0: white).

GltfSource.doc: A model file placed as is, at the marker's position and yaw (no scale: use a prefab instance for that). path is under the asset folder (models/features/x.gltf).

Body.doc: A static box collider on a placed model (a prefab instance): sx x sy x sz metres, its middle ox, oy, oz from the instance's origin along its own axes (so it turns and tilts with it).

Bob.doc: Bobs up and down height metres at hz bobs a second, phase radians along (a floating blimp).

Pad.doc: A surf course pad (the box is the marker's size): stage `stage` (from 0) starts here, or the course's finish.

Ridge.doc: One point of a surf ramp's ridge: ramp `ramp` of stage `stage`, point `order` along it. A smooth curve runs through them.

Wedge.doc: A wedge-shaped static collider (a surf kicker): the marker's box, low at -z rising to its full height at +z, turned by the marker's yaw.

SpeedGap.doc: A speed-check gap follows ramp `ramp` of stage `stage` of the surf course: the next ramp is only reached carrying speed.

RampLook.doc: How surf stage `stage`'s ramps look (they are drawn from their ridge points): colour r, g, b, glow (emissive times colour), roughness, metalness. Without one: dark blue steel.

Arcade.doc: A Wonderland arcade machine marker: `game` is skeeball (a lane's ball start, `id` = lane), skeeball_hole (that lane's hole worth `points`, `radius` m), dartboard (board centre, facing = the marker's yaw, `id` = board) or oche (that board's throw line).
